questions.question: Describe a hardware test or electronics-debugging project where you diagnosed a failure down to the component level. What tools, measurements, and reasoning did you use?
In your role at Zoom, how did you develop or maintain the test automation framework using Bash, DOS batch scripts, terminal macros, Linux, and Unix file systems?

This role supports embedded controllers for image-capture systems. What experience do you have programming electronic components or assemblies, and how did you validate that programming was successful?
Walk me through how you read a digital circuit schematic when troubleshooting a board. How do you trace signals, power rails, resets, clocks, and interfaces?
What types of electronic assemblies have you stress-tested in environmental chambers, and what failures or performance issues were you trying to identify?
Describe your experience creating and revising programming and testing procedures. How did you ensure the documentation was clear enough for manufacturing or other technicians to follow consistently?
When repairing a PCB at the component level, how do you distinguish between a failed component, a soldering or assembly defect, and an upstream circuit issue?
What experience have you had working with PCB layouts, board routing, or providing layout feedback based on test and debug findings?

This position uses C for microcontroller firmware and may involve ARM devices, FPGAs, and tools such as Code Composer Studio. What exposure have you had to C programming, embedded development environments, or programmable digital devices?
Describe a time you led a testing effort by scheduling work, tracking progress, and training others. How did you handle changing priorities or technical blockers?
